prerequisites: Knowledge acquired in previous courses in mathematics and circuit theory.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the frequency representation of deterministic signals.
Understanding of the concept of noise as a stochastic process.
Knowledge of the simplest techniques for information transmission.
Ability to analyze deterministic and random signals and calculate their fundamental properties (spectrum, bandwidth, power, or energy).
Ability to define the transmission parameters, design, and performance during the operation of analog and digital transmission systems in their simplest form.

syllabus_topics: Definition, classification, and properties of signals; signal energy and power.
Impulse response and properties of linear systems. Eigenfunctions and frequency response.
Frequency-domain analysis of deterministic signals. Fourier series representations and component orthogonality. Parseval's theorem.
Energy Spectral Density (ESD) and Power Spectral Density (PSD). Fourier transform and its properties. Transfer functions, causality conditions, and filtering.

Waveform correlation, autocorrelation, cross-correlation, and power correlation. Wiener
Khinchin theorem. Autocorrelation of periodic functions.

Fundamentals of modulation: baseband signal, carrier signal, and modulated signal. Frequency translation and baseband equivalent representation of modulated signals. Overview of analog modulations: frequency (FM), phase (PM), and amplitude modulation (AM) with unsuppressed carrier.

Probability theory: random experiments, sample space, random events, random variables, and probability definitions. Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) and Probability Density Function (PDF). Statistical characterization of random variables; Gaussian distribution. Independent and uncorrelated random variables. Central Limit Theorem and Bayes' Theorem. Random processes and characterization: stationary and ergodic processes. Noise modeling as a stochastic process.
Sampling theorem, quantization, and signal reconstruction. Nyquist criterion. Digital signals and digital modulation schemes. Baseband and passband representations, power spectrum. Matched filter.
Performance of telecommunication systems in noise; Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR). Performance of digital modulations and Bit Error Rate (BER).
The MATLAB environment and its applications in signal theory and communications. Practical implementation of telecommunication functions in MATLAB.
assessment_rules: The examination consists of a mandatory written test and an optional oral exam. The written test includes at least two problems and an open-ended theoretical question, with a maximum score of 27/30. The oral exam is optional if the written test score is sufficient, but mandatory to pass if the written test score is between 16 and 17/30. If the student, with a sufficient grade in the written exam, decides not to take the oral exam, the final grade remains that of the written exam, limited to 22/30 if the written score is higher. In the case of an oral exam, the final grade will be determined starting from the written exam grade, applying a variation according to the preparation ascertained on the topics of the oral exam. The oral exam allows passing the exam even with a written test score between 16 and 17 if the final grade is at least 18. The maximum attainable score is 30 with honors.
